An integer with four positive divisors is p^3 or pq for distinct primes p,q. The first case has divisor sum (p+1)(p²+1); the sums at p=11 and p=13 are 1464 and 2380, so none lies in the interval. In the pq case the sum is (p+1)(q+1). If one prime is 2, the only possible interval values are 2010 and 2016, giving the nonprime candidates q=669 and q=671. If both primes are odd, the sum must be divisible by 4, leaving 2012 and 2016. Since 2012/4=503 is prime, 2012 cannot have both even factors at least 4. But 2016=(3+1)(503+1), so m=3·503 has divisors 1,3,503,1509 summing to 2016. Exactly one number is nice.

Let BC=x and CD=AD=y. The consecutive right angles make AB and CD parallel. The viable configuration gives y²=x²+(y−2)², hence x²=4(y−1). The opposite-side configuration would instead require y²=x²+(y+2)², which is impossible. Integrality forces x=2k and y=k²+1 for an integer k≥1. Thus p=2k²+2k+4, strictly increasing with k. At k=31, p=1988<2015; at k=32, p=2116>2015. Every k from 1 through 31 constructs a valid quadrilateral, so there are 31 distinct values.

A point (x,y) is on an allowed path exactly when |x+3|+|x−3|+|y−2|+|y+2|≤20: this is the shortest axis-parallel path length through that point, and it is attainable. Equivalently, dist(x,[-3,3])+dist(y,[-2,2])≤5. For each of the five rows −2≤y≤2 there are 17 integer x-values. At y=±(2+j), j=1,...,5, there are 17−2j values per row. The total is 5·17+2(15+13+11+9+7)=195. The alternative decomposition gives 35+50+70+40=195 and is also valid.

Write s=sin x and c=cos x. In the stated interval, s>0, c<0, and c+s<0. All points lie on y=u², where a chord through parameters u,v has slope u+v. The extreme parameters are cot x and sin x; the middle parameters are cos x and tan x, in either order. The only possible parallel pair therefore requires cot x+sin x=cos x+tan x. Multiplying by sc and cancelling the nonzero c−s gives c+s=sc. For z=sc, squaring yields z²=1+2z. Since z<0, z=1−√2, not 1+√2. Thus sin(2x)=2z=2−2√2. This solution lies in the stated interval and gives four distinct vertices.
